page_index.note: The PDF holds TWO complete 14-sheet sets. PDF pages 1-14 are an older set (title-block dates May 2023); PDF pages 15-28 are the newer set (dates 3-5 June 2023). This extract uses the June set (pages 15-28). All page numbers below are PDF page numbers (1-based), with the schematic sheet number in brackets.

page_index.16: [sheet 2] Power (input, buck regulators, 3V3, VCCIO, USB Type-C)
page_index.17: [sheet 3] STM32F4XXVET6 (MCU, 74HCT365A buffers U9/U11/U12/U13, EEPROM, SWD, BOOT0/RESET)
page_index.old_vs_new_diff: A word-level diff of old vs new pages shows the same MCU pin labels on both MCU sheets (p3 vs p17). The new set adds SW2 (DIP-2: PI_SCL->BOOT0, PI_SDA->RESET), SW4/J80 (BOOT0 button), SW3 replaces SW1 (TC_KEY_4P) on reset, and PI_SDA/PI_SCL on Pi header J22 pins 4/6. In the old set, J22 pins 2/4/6/8 are no-connects. LED colours and resistor values also changed.

drivers_common.buffers: Four 74HCT365A (U9, U11, U12, U13), VCC = DC_5V, EN1/EN2 (pins 1, 15) tied to GND, so they are always enabled. Every MCU EN/STEP/DIR pin feeds an A input through a 1k series resistor, and the Y output drives the socket port. U9 serves X and Y, U11 serves Z and E0, U12 serves E1 and E2, U13 serves E3 and E4 (p17). CS, MOSI, SCK and MISO are NOT buffered.
drivers_common.polarity: The 74HCT365A is drawn as a non-inverting buffer. The module ENA pin is drawn active-low (overbar), with a 10k pull-up to VCCIO on each driver sheet (R173, R175, ... R187).
drivers_common.logic_supply: Driver VDD and jumper pull-ups use VCCIO. On p16, VCCIO comes from +5V through bead FB2. Alternative U5 ME6217C33M5G (3.3V LDO) is marked '/NC'.
drivers_common.socket_to_refdes_mapping: UNRESOLVED. The instance pages are MD1 (p21), MD2 (p22), MD3 (p23), MD4 (p24), MD5 (p25), MD6 (p26), MD7 (p27), MD8 (p28). MD1 and MD2 are the only HV instances, so they are X and Y, but no page says which is which. No page names which of MD3..MD8 is Z or E0..E4. MCU pins per socket come from p15 and p17 and do not depend on this mapping.

jumper_block: Each socket has a 12-pin 'JUMPER_4X3' (J64, J66, J68, J70, J72, J74, J76, J78 on pp.21-28; same on every instance). It has four rows A-D, each with a center pin (1-4), an 'x1' pin (5-8) and an 'x2' pin (9-12). Row A: center pin1 -> module MS1 (pin2); A1 (pin5) -> 4.7k (RN quad) -> VCCIO; A2 (pin9) -> SPI4.MOSI. Row B: center pin2 -> module MS2 (pin3); B1 (pin6) -> 4.7k -> VCCIO; B2 (pin10) -> SPI4.SCK. Row C: center pin3 -> module MS3 (pin4); C1 (pin7) -> 4.7k -> VCCIO; C2 (pin11) -> 100R (R188..R195) -> sheet port SPI4_CS -> that socket's MCU CS pin. Row D: center pin4 -> net 'CGF0' -> module RST (pin5); D1 (pin8) -> 4.7k -> VCCIO; D2 (pin12) -> SPI4.MISO. Shorting center to x1 pulls MSx/RST high to VCCIO, which is standalone microstep config. Shorting center to x2 routes the SPI bus (MOSI->MS1, SCK->MS2, CS->MS3, MISO->RST position). With no jumper on a row, that pin floats. The only MCU line that reaches MS3 (pin 4, the PDN/UART position on UART modules) is the socket's own CS pin through row C. No UART-specific labeling or TX/RX bridge resistor is drawn. The physical 4x3 pin layout and silkscreen are not shown. Separately, on p15, 2-pin jumpers JP1..JP6 connect the X, Y, Z, E0, E1, E2 driver DIAG outputs to the X_MIN, Y_MIN, Z_MIN, Z_MAX, Y_MAX, X_MAX endstop nets respectively. E3 and E4 have no DIAG jumper.

i2c.pi_i2c_lines: J22 pin4 PI_SDA and pin6 PI_SCL go (p17) only to SW2 'SW DIP-2': PI_SCL -> switch -> BOOT0, PI_SDA -> switch -> RESET. On the MCU sheet they are NOT wired to PB8/PB9, although p15 shows italic hints 'PB8'/'PB9' next to the PI_SCL/PI_SDA ports (see unresolved)

boot.BOOT0: MCU pin 94 BOOT0 net, R165 10k to GND. SW4 pushbutton from VDD to BOOT0, with J80 (CON2) in parallel. SW2 DIP switch 1 connects PI_SCL (J22 pin6) to BOOT0. J62 SWD header pin2 = BOOT0.
boot.NRST: MCU pin 14 NRST -> R166 100R -> net RESET. RESET has R157 100k pull-up to VDD and C71 100nF to GND. SW3 pushbutton RESET -> GND with J63 (CON2) in parallel. SW2 DIP switch 2 connects PI_SDA (J22 pin4) to RESET. RESET also goes to EXP2 pin3 and J25 pin8.
boot.BOOT1: PB2 (pin 37) has R139 10k to GND. This pin is also PWM_FAN2.
boot.SWD_header: J62 (CON_5): 1 +3V3, 2 BOOT0, 3 GND, 4 PA13/SWDIO, 5 PA14/SWCLK. PA13 and PA14 are also PWM_FAN0 and PWM_FAN1.
boot.clock: Y1 12MHz/10ppm on PH0-OSC_IN (pin 12) and PH1-OSC_OUT (pin 13), C86/C87 16pF
boot.older_revision: Pages 1-14 (May 2023) have no SW2, SW4 or J80. Reset there is SW1 (TC_KEY_4P) with J63.

other.PD3_debug_led: PD3 also drives D63 (BLUE) through R153 1.5k to GND (net labels DEBUG_LED and Neo-pixel on the same wire), p17
other.PB2_BOOT1: PB2 = PWM_FAN2 with R139 10k pull-down (BOOT1), p17
other.SWD_shared_with_fans: PA13 (SWDIO) = PWM_FAN0 and PA14 (SWCLK) = PWM_FAN1. Both are on J62. The MCU symbol lists no timer channel on PA13 or PA14 ('PA13/JTMS-SWDIO/EVENTOUT', 'PA14/JTCK-SWCLK/EVENTOUT'), p17
other.JTAG_pins_used_as_heaters: PB3 (symbol PB3/JTDO/TRACESWO) = E2_Heater; PB4 (symbol PB4/NJTRST) = BED_Heater, p17
other.BL_PWM: J36 pin3 BL_PWM is the Y_MAX net = PA2, p20
other.probe: J40 PROBE <- D16 BAT85 <- Z_MAX (PA3). See endstops, p20
other.mcu_supply: VDD = VBAT = 3V3_MCU (one net). VDDA through bead FB3. VCAP_1 (pin 48) C72 4.7uF, VCAP_2 (pin 73) C73 4.7uF. Pin 49 VSS_3 -> R162 0R -> GND. That matches the F446 LQFP100 option in the sheet's 'Figure 1' note, p17
other.power_select_misc: J33 (+24V/GND) and J34 (+12V/GND) are 2x2 power outputs, p20. Fan voltage-select headers J10/J11/J12 and RGB headers J57/J58/J16 each offer DC_5V / +12V / +24V, p18
other.unused_gpio: None. All 79 GPIOs of the LQFP100 symbol (PA0-15, PB0-15 without PB11, PC0-15, PD0-15, PE0-15) carry a net; PH0/PH1 are the crystal

unresolved: Driver-instance mapping: the per-socket sheets (pp.21-28) do not print which axis they belong to. MD1/MD2 (with J64/J65, J66/J67, R188/R189, RN3/RN4) are the two HV instances (X and Y) but not identified individually. Which of MD3..MD8 (J68..J79, R190..R195, RN5..RN10) is Z or E0..E4 is not stated. Page order is not proof, because sheet order could be alphabetical by instance name. MCU pin assignments are unaffected; only refdes-to-socket labels are.

Jumper block physical arrangement: JUMPER_4X3 is shown electrically (center / x1 pull-up / x2 SPI per row) but the physical pin layout and silkscreen are not drawn. UART (PDN_UART) mode is not labelled anywhere. The only MCU line reaching module pin 4 (MS3) is the socket CS through row C, and no TX/RX bridge resistor is drawn. Whether that CS line is meant for single-wire UART cannot be confirmed from the schematic.

PI_SCL/PI_SDA vs PB8/PB9: p15 shows italic hints 'PB8'/'PB9' beside the PI_SCL/PI_SDA ports, but on p17 those ports connect only to SW2 (DIP) -> BOOT0/RESET, and PB8/PB9 connect only to the EEPROM, J7 and pull-ups. No net joins PI_SCL to PB8 or PI_SDA to PB9. The connectivity (p17) has been taken as authoritative.

Endstop voltage jumpers JP10-JP14: an unlabeled blue bar (no refdes or value) is drawn between the pin-1 supply (+3V3 for MIN, DC_5V for MAX) and pin 2 (connector V+). It looks like a default short (net-tie or solder bridge). If it is populated, moving the jumper to the +24V position would short +24V to +3V3/DC_5V. Its population status cannot be determined.

Population options: VCCIO is taken as +5V via FB2 because U5 (3.3V LDO) is marked 'ME6217C33M5G/NC'. MOS_PWR is taken as +12V because R30 is 0R and R31 is 'NC'. The note 'R27=0R (446) / R27=4.7uF, C32=NC (405/407)' refers to refdes that do not appear on the drawing (R162/C72 are drawn), so the fitted MCU variant can only be inferred (drawn as the F446 option).
J62 SWD header: the rotated GND symbol on pin 3 visually overlaps the pin-2 (BOOT0) and pin-4 (SWDIO) wires. It is interpreted as GND on pin 3 only (net labels BOOT0 on pin 2, PA13/SWDIO on pin 4).
FAN3, FAN4, FAN5 do not exist as nets. The schematic has only FAN0-FAN2 plus three MOSFET-switched RGB channels (PB7/PB6/PB5 -> J59/J60/J61 and J17). Any FAN3-5 naming is outside this schematic.

Endstop pull-ups: no pull-up resistor is drawn on X_MIN (PB14), Y_MIN (PB13), X_MAX (PA1) or Y_MAX (PA2). Z_MIN has R85 10k and Z_MAX has R88 10k to +3V3. Whether firmware must enable internal pull-ups is outside the schematic.

Board revision: the PDF contains two revisions (pp.1-14 May 2023, pp.15-28 June 2023). The MCU pin labels match between them, but the BOOT0/RESET/Pi-I2C circuitry differs. The schematic cannot tell which revision a given physical board is.
